title: How OneCoin sold a coin that never existed

hook.belief: Nobody would pour real money into a coin that does not exist; millions of buyers must have been sold real technology.
hook.gap: If the coin was never real, what were millions of people actually buying?

scenes.narration: Four billion dollars for a coin that never existed? OneCoin took that much from victims worldwide.
scenes.visual_intent: A gold coin spins up as an investment, then is shown to be a flat drawing with nothing behind it.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A glowing gold coin turns edge-on and is revealed as a paper-thin cutout with nothing behind it.

facts.claim: OneCoin took in more than $4 billion from victims worldwide between 2014 and 2016.

scenes.narration: Bitcoin runs on a public ledger. Many computers hold the same copy, so a fake balance gets rejected.
scenes.visual_intent: One ledger page is copied to many machines, so a forged line is caught by every copy at once.
scenes.visualMetaphor: One ledger page fans out into a wall of identical copies; a forged row flashes red on every copy.

facts.claim: Bitcoin records transactions in a public ledger (a blockchain) that many independent nodes hold and verify, so a forged balance is rejected.
facts.source: Nakamoto, S. (2008). Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System. https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf

scenes.narration: OneCoin kept its ledger private. [PAUSE 0.9s] Prosecutors say it had no true blockchain, and its bosses handed out coins that existed nowhere.
scenes.visual_intent: The wall of public copies goes dark, leaving one locked book that someone simply writes numbers into.
scenes.visualMetaphor: The wall of copies goes dark; one padlocked ledger book remains and a hand writes balances into it.

facts.claim: Prosecutors say OneCoin had no true, verifiable blockchain.
Greenwood and Ignatova allocated to members OneCoins that did not exist even in OneCoin's purported private blockchain.

scenes.narration: So who sold it? Ruja Ignatova. The press called her the Cryptoqueen. In 2016 she took the stage at Wembley Arena and called OneCoin the bitcoin killer.
scenes.visual_intent: An arena lights up for a pitch from an empty, faceless podium; the founder herself is never drawn.
scenes.visualMetaphor: Arena spotlights sweep and lock on an empty podium while rows of phone lights rise in the crowd.

facts.claim: In the summer of 2016 Ruja Ignatova took the stage at Wembley Arena and promoted OneCoin as the bitcoin killer.
Ruja Ignatova was dubbed the Cryptoqueen.

scenes.narration: A stage only sells one crowd, so OneCoin paid its members to recruit new buyers. [PAUSE 0.6s] The coin was the excuse. The recruit was the product.
scenes.visual_intent: A recruitment tree spreads downward while the money from every new buyer climbs to the top.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A recruitment tree grows downward; money climbs every branch to a single crown at the top.

facts.claim: OneCoin members bought OneCoin packages and were paid commissions for recruiting others to buy packages, a pyramid scheme.

scenes.narration: Here's the catch. Nobody could check OneCoin's books. So buyers trusted the friend who sold it, and that friend was paid to be trusted.
scenes.visual_intent: A relay of hands passes one coin down the line, each taking a commission slip, beside a ledger chained shut.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A relay of hands passes a coin down a line, each taking a commission slip, beside a ledger that stays chained shut.

facts.claim: Prosecutors say OneCoin had no true, verifiable blockchain; its records were a purported private blockchain.
OneCoin members were paid commissions for recruiting others to buy packages.

scenes.narration: Then in October 2017, Ruja boarded a flight to Athens and vanished. [PAUSE 0.9s] What her buyers held was a number in a private book.
scenes.visual_intent: A torn boarding pass and a flight line that fades out over the sea before it reaches Athens.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A boarding pass tears in two while a dotted flight line toward Athens fades out over the sea.

facts.claim: On 25 October 2017 Ruja Ignatova boarded a flight from Sofia to Athens and has not been seen since (as of the January 2023 report).
OneCoins were allocated to members in OneCoin's own private records and did not exist on any true blockchain.
